title: PlayStation 5 için yayınlanan Relapse adlı yeni yazılım kırma yöntemi korsanlık riskini artırıyor
summary: Kotaku'nun aktardığına göre, PlayStation 5 konsollarını hedefleyen yeni bir yazılım kırma yöntemi, en son sürüm hariç neredeyse tüm cihazlarda çalışıyor.
body:
Kotaku'nun aktardığına göre, PlayStation 5 için geliştirilen **Relapse** adlı yeni yazılım kırma (jailbreak) yöntemi, şirketin güvenliği açısından büyük bir açık oluşturuyor. Temmuz ayında yayınlanan sistem yazılımından bu yana neredeyse tüm PS5 konsollarında çalışabilen bu yeni açık, sadece birkaç hafta önce yayınlanan 14.00.00 sürümünün dışındaki tüm cihazları etkiliyor. Bu durum, piyasadaki pek çok konsolun ve hatta PlayStation 5 Pro modellerinin bu yönteme karşı savunmasız kalmasına neden oluyor. Açığın bir dakikadan kısa bir sürede tamamlanabildiği belirtiliyor.

## Korsanlık ve güncel oyunlar üzerindeki etkileri

Kotaku'nun haberine göre, modern korsan PS5 oyunları genellikle kullanıcıların güncel bir sistem yazılımı çalıştırmasını gerektiriyor. Relapse yöntemi, temmuz sonundaki sürümde çalıştığı için 16 Eylül'de yayınlanan 14.00.00 güncellemesinden önce çıkan tüm oyunları potansiyel olarak riske atıyor. Örneğin, 15 Eylül'de çıkan Marvel’s Wolverine oyununun bu durumdan etkilendiği ifade ediliyor. Reddit üzerindeki kullanıcılar, yakın zamanda çıkan The Witcher 3: Remastered oyununun da bu açık sayesinde çalıştırılabildiğini bildiriyor. Sony'nin bu duruma karşı kısa vadede yeni bir güncelleme yayınlaması bekleniyor.

**Neden önemli?** Yeni yazılım kırma yöntemi, konsol pazarında korsan oyun oynama ihtimalini artırırken Sony'nin bu güvenlik açığını nasıl kapatacağı henüz bilinmiyor.

source_texts.title: A New PS5 Jailbreak May Have Just Opened The Floodgates To Piracy
source_texts.summary: According to those who have installed the new Relapse exploit, it works with everything from Marvel's Wolverine to The Witcher 3: Remastered
source_texts.text:
Hackers have uncovered a new jailbreaking method for the PlayStation 5. That wouldn’t normally big a huge deal. Several exploits taking control of the console have been making the rounds for quite some time now. Unfortunately for Sony, the new âRelapseâ jailbreak exploit works on every PS5 firmware version, bar one: version 14.00.00, which is less than two weeks old. That makes it a much bigger vulnerability for the company to deal with, and one that could have major implications for piracy on the platform.Â
So, why is this a big deal? There are two reasons: the first being that those who purchased PlayStation 5s more recently, which come pre-installed with more recent firmware, will still be able to access the new exploit. Basically, that means that any retail PS5s, including PS5 Pros, that have been on shelves for longer than a couple weeks will be vulnerable to the âRelapseâ jailbreak method.Â
The second reason is a much bigger issue for Sony. Modern pirated PS5 games often require users to be running a more up-to-date version of the system firmware in order for them to boot. Likewise, if you want to update a pirated game, for either quality-of-life reasons or to take advantage of DLC releases, you also usually need to install the most recent firmware.
 New PlayStation 5 jailbreak just dropped. Every PS5 console can now be jailbroken except ones updated in the past week or so. Huge. pic.twitter.com/6FXb4SAcPv
— Lance McDonald (@manfightdragon) September 29, 2026
As the âRelapseâ jailbreak method works on PS5 systems running v26.05-13.60.00, which was released in late July, that means every game that was released before the 14.00.00 update, which dropped on September 16, 2026, could potentially be compromised by pirates.Â
Marvel’s Wolverine, for example, shipped on September 15. Adding insult to injury is that the “Relapse” jailbreak method can reportedly be completed in under a minute.Â
Of course, Marvel’s Wolverine isnât the only recent game affected here. Users on the r/PS5_Jailbreak subreddit are reporting that The Witcher 3: Remastered, which just came out today, can also somehow run using the Relapse jailbreak. Expect a new firmware update to cut off this exploitâs longevity in the immediate future, but for now it’s unclear how Sony can put the genie back in the bottle for all of the PS5 games and updates already released.Â

source_texts.title: 'The Witcher 3 Remastered' Pirates Are Encouraging Each Other To Buy It Instead
source_texts.summary: Even The Witcher 3 pirates on PC feel bad for not supporting developer CD Projekt Red and its approach to DLC and DRM
source_texts.text:
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered is officially out on PC now, which also means it's available on piracy sites. This isn't a case of a lightning-fast game crack, but rather the inevitability of what happens when a video game is released without digital rights management (DRM) software. For most companies, this piracy scenario would be a nightmare on launch day. CD Projekt Red, however, released a game like this on purpose — and it's earned immense favor with people who might otherwise play without spending a dime.
In communities like Crack Watch, some people are unrepentantly taking the game without paying for it. Most people, however, tell each other to financially support CD Projekt Red and its business practices.
"Honestly CDPR are the most consumer-friendly company around I would encourage everyone to buy it," one top-voted comment said.
"Even the pirates recognize & honor games like these," another said.
"Feels bad to pirate this gem ngl," yet another admitted.
CD Projekt Red's generosity impresses even pirates
Beyond the lack of DRM, pirates point to CD Projekt Red's ongoing generosity toward its fans. When The Witcher 3 was first released, the developer made some DLC completely free. Then, when the studio released paid content, the expansions were hefty yet surprisingly cheap. Players felt like they got a lot of bang for their buck, especially when the base game was already a massive RPG experience.
The developer lost some of this goodwill after the messy release of Cyberpunk 2077. That sour disposition softened after CD Projekt Red spent years reworking the game and releasing strong DLC content. Years later, when the developer announced The Witcher 3 Remastered, the company officially came back into the gaming world's good graces. It helps that, for most people, the new version of the game and its astonishing number of quality-of-life improvements will be a completely free download. And for those who don't have it, pirates would like to remind you that it's still not a good excuse to steal the game.
"I would encourage everyone to buy it there's a 50% sale on right now," one pirate said.
Many say that they won't be downloading the crack because they pirated it before — and the experience was so good that they eventually chose to buy it. Actually, the game has been so heavily discounted before that many pirates are surprised that there are people out there who haven't already bought it.
"IS THERE A SINGLE PERSON on the planet, who doesn't have this in some form?" one pirate wrote. "Like the game is constantly on heavy, like HEAVY discounts."
Even with a discount, buying the game isn't an option for everyone. With the current state of PC gaming, though, some of these folks may not be able to play it anyway.
"Now I just need to be able to pirate a 5080 or better to even run this with the recommended specs," one pirate joked.
